title: Middle Eocene Climatic Optimum
summary: The Middle Eocene Climatic Optimum was a warming episode with peak warmth placed at 40.0 Ma, lasting about 500,000 years in total and under 100,000 years at its peak. Oxygen-isotope records indicate roughly 4–6 °C of warming in surface and deep waters at study sites; a southwest Pacific record shows 3–6 °C of sea-surface warming alongside a 2–3-fold CO2 increase.

uncertainty.note: Peak warming at 40.0 Ma (Bohaty et al. 2009), total duration about 500 ka; Bijl et al. (2010) say ~40 Ma. Years are Ma with no 1950 offset; start and end are both the peak.

as_recorded.value: Middle Eocene Climatic Optimum (MECO; ~40 million years ago)

where.modern_name: Global event; pin at the Pacific Ocean (Bijl et al. record is from the southwest Pacific)

importance.justification: A transient warming within the long Eocene cooling, tied to a CO2 rise.

sources.title: Coupled greenhouse warming and deep-sea acidification in the middle Eocene (abstract of Bohaty et al., Paleoceanography 24:PA2207)
